# Shroom Labs

> Shroom Labs is a library of researched mushroom grow profiles. Apply them from a Hub to a chamber running OpenShrooly.

Site: https://shroomlabs.io

## Culinary Profiles

- [Beech / Buna Shimeji](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/beech-shimeji.html): Beech / Buna Shimeji fruits at 15 °C and 90% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 40 days from start to fruit. Clustered beech mushroom. Cool, humid, and a little less fresh air than oysters.
- [Blue Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/blue-oyster.html): Blue Oyster fruits at 14 °C and 87% humidity with plenty of fresh air and 12 h light. About 25 days from start to fruit. Cool-preferring oyster. Deep color holds better below 18 °C.
- [Button / Cremini](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/button-cremini.html): Button / Cremini fruits at 16 °C and 88% humidity with moderate fresh air and 0 h light. About 36 days from start to fruit. Compost + casing species. Low light, cool fruiting, casing required.
- [Chestnut Mushroom](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/chestnut.html): Chestnut Mushroom fruits at 15 °C and 92% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 34 days from start to fruit. Clustered woodlover. Cool fruiting and high humidity keep caps glossy.
- [Cordyceps militaris](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/cordyceps-militaris.html): Cordyceps militaris fruits at 18 °C and 84% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 57 days from start to fruit. Grown on supplemented grain/rice, not logs. Wants 12/12 light once orange initials show.
- [Elm Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/elm-oyster.html): Elm Oyster fruits at 15 °C and 86% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 31 days from start to fruit. Not a true Pleurotus. Cooler fruiting, meaty single fruits more than oyster clusters.
- [Enoki](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/enoki.html): Enoki fruits at 15 °C and 93% humidity with little fresh air and 0 h light. About 43 days from start to fruit. Needs cold fruiting and little fresh air for supermarket-long stems.
- [Golden Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/golden-oyster.html): Golden Oyster fruits at 21 °C and 87% humidity with plenty of fresh air and 12 h light. About 24 days from start to fruit. Warm oyster with dense golden clusters. Needs plenty of fresh air to keep stems short.
- [King Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/king-oyster.html): King Oyster fruits at 15 °C and 82% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 38 days from start to fruit. Thick-stem oyster. Cooler, slightly drier, and less fresh air than cluster oysters.
- [King Oyster: thick-stem method](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/king-oyster-thick-stem.html): Paid culinary Profile, $2.99. About 43 days from start to fruit. Paid example recipe: cooler, drier fruiting to favor thick stems.
- [Lion's Mane](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/lions-mane.html): Lion's Mane fruits at 17 °C and 90% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 33 days from start to fruit. Tooth fungus. Moderate fresh air, since too much air yellows the spines.
- [Maitake](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/maitake.html): Maitake fruits at 16 °C and 88% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 54 days from start to fruit. Slow woodlover. Primordia look like brains; do not dry them out.
- [Nameko](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/nameko.html): Nameko fruits at 14 °C and 93% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 39 days from start to fruit. Cool, very wet fruiting. The slime coat is normal.
- [Pearl Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/pearl-oyster.html): Pearl Oyster fruits at 16 °C and 88% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 29 days from start to fruit. Forgiving beginner oyster. Fast, lots of fresh air, cool-to-room fruiting.
- [Pink Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/pink-oyster.html): Pink Oyster fruits at 24 °C and 86% humidity with plenty of fresh air and 12 h light. About 20 days from start to fruit. Tropical oyster. Wants warmth; stalls and fades in a cold room.
- [Pioppino](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/pioppino.html): Pioppino fruits at 16 °C and 86% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 31 days from start to fruit. Black poplar mushroom. Cool fruiting; keep the surface less wet than oysters.
- [Reishi](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/reishi.html): Reishi fruits at 23 °C and 85% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 77 days from start to fruit. Antlers under high CO2, then consoles when fresh air increases.
- [Shiitake](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/shiitake.html): Shiitake fruits at 16 °C and 85% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 74 days from start to fruit. Needs a full colonize + browning rest, then a cold shock before fruiting.
- [Turkey Tail](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/turkey-tail.html): Turkey Tail fruits at 20 °C and 86% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 78 days from start to fruit. Thin polypore. Long fruiting, lots of fresh air, not a thick-fleshed edible.
- [Wine Cap](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/wine-cap.html): Wine Cap fruits at 17 °C and 85% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 40 days from start to fruit. Best as an outdoor bed mushroom. Indoor profile is a climate approximation only.
- [Wood Ear](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/wood-ear.html): Wood Ear fruits at 24 °C and 92% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 38 days from start to fruit. Warm, wet jelly fungus. High humidity matters more than light intensity.

## Off-menu Profiles

Reference conditions for research and education only. Not sold. Grow Coach does not cover these.

Psilocybin mushrooms are illegal to grow, possess, or sell in most countries and under US federal law. This information is published for educational, research and harm-reduction purposes only. Check the laws where you live. Shroom Labs does not sell spores, cultures or psilocybin products.

- [B+](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/b-plus.html): B+ fruits at 21 °C and 89% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 32 days from start to fruit. Forgiving cubensis strain with a slightly wider temperature window.
- [Golden Teacher](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/golden-teacher.html): Golden Teacher fruits at 22 °C and 90% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 32 days from start to fruit. Common cubensis strain. Reference conditions for research and education only.
- [Penis Envy](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/penis-envy.html): Penis Envy fruits at 22 °C and 90% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 50 days from start to fruit. Slower cubensis. Same climate band as Golden Teacher with longer stage timers.
- [Psilocybe cyanescens](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/p-cyanescens.html): Psilocybe cyanescens fruits at 15 °C and 90% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 52 days from start to fruit. Cool-weather woodlover. Indoor chambers are a poor substitute for outdoor beds.
- [Psilocybe natalensis](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/p-natalensis.html): Psilocybe natalensis fruits at 23 °C and 90% humidity with moderate fresh air and 12 h light. About 29 days from start to fruit. Cubensis-adjacent climate; often described as a bit more vigorous.

## Microscopy and research resources

These are plain links to other sites. We do not endorse these vendors or publishers, we earn nothing from them, and the links carry no referral codes or tracking.

Spore laws vary by state and country, and some US states ban spores outright. Where they are sold, spores are sold for microscopy only.

- [PNW Spore](https://pnwspore.com/). US vendor of spore prints and syringes, sold for microscopy.
- [Sporeworks](https://sporeworks.com/). Long-running US spore catalog, sold for microscopy.
- [National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIH)](https://nida.nih.gov/research-topics/psilocybin-magic-mushrooms). US government overview of psilocybin, its effects, and current research.
- [Johns Hopkins Center for Psychedelic and Consciousness Research](https://www.hopkinspsychedelic.org/publications). Peer-reviewed psilocybin studies from Johns Hopkins Medicine.
